# AGENT PROMPT — Network Automation System: wire it to GNS3 (and Packet Tracer) and make it work end-to-end

You are a senior network-automation / full-stack engineer working directly in my repository
(unzipped from `Network_Automation_System_GNS3.zip`). You can read files, edit code, run commands,
run tests and (on my machine) talk to a real GNS3 server. Work autonomously, but report honestly.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. HOW TO WORK (read first)

1. Read the repo before changing anything. Do not trust this prompt's file list blindly; verify it.
2. Begin with a SHORT PLAN (max 15 lines), then execute phase by phase (section 6).
3. After each phase: run the tests / commands, then tell me what you verified vs. what you assumed.
4. Never claim something works unless you executed it. Separate "Verified" from "Not verified".
5. Prefer minimal, targeted changes. Extend the project; do not rewrite it.
6. Explain each non-trivial change in 1-2 lines (what and why).
7. If a decision is mine to make (e.g. which GNS3 image, which Windows adapter name), ask ONCE,
   batch your questions, and keep working on everything else meanwhile.
8. Ask before anything destructive (deleting the DB, deleting GNS3 projects, force-pushing).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

"Network Configuration Automation System": a web app to manage Cisco IOS devices.

Stack
- Backend: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy (SQLite `backend/database.db`), Netmiko (SSH), optional Ansible, entry `backend/main.py`.
- Frontend: React (Vite) in `frontend/`; the built `frontend/dist` is served by FastAPI (catch-all route in `main.py`).
- Ansible: `ansible/inventory/`, `ansible/playbooks/*.yml`.
- Built-in mock Cisco SSH server: `backend/app/mock_cisco/simulator.py` (port 2222) for demos.
- Launchers: `run.bat` (demo / simulator), `run_gns3.bat` (real devices + GNS3 auto-provisioning).
- Docs: `docs/GNS3_SETUP.md`.

Features: device inventory, test connection, backup/restore of running-config, config deployment
(Ansible with Netmiko fallback), drift detection, verification checks, audit logs, reports, dashboard.

Platform: I run Windows (Egypt, Arabic/English UI users). GNS3 2.2.x is on the same machine.
Ansible does not run natively on Windows (needs WSL/Linux) -> Netmiko is the fallback.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. WHAT HAS ALREADY BEEN CHANGED (by a previous session — review it critically)

A. Simulator vs real mode  (`backend/app/services/netmiko_engine.py`, `backend/main.py`)
   - Env `SIMULATOR_MODE`: `off` (default) = real devices; `on` = legacy demo.
   - In real mode: NO redirect of 192.168.1.x to the mock, NO fake "Simulated" success,
     failures are reported honestly (Offline / FAILED). `fetch_running_config` raises
     `DeviceConnectionError`, mapped to HTTP 502 by an exception handler in `main.py`.
   - Mock SSH server only starts when `SIMULATOR_MODE=on`.
   - `verify_device_status` now checks the real running-config (VLAN, SSH v2, trunk, port-security, mgmt IP)
     instead of always returning PASS.
   - Netmiko connections enter enable mode automatically; longer timeouts (IOSv boots slowly).

B. Ansible  (`ansible/playbooks/deploy_config.yml`, `backend/app/services/ansible_engine.py`)
   - `hosts: target_devices` (matched nothing) -> `hosts: "{{ target_devices | default('all') }}"`.
   - `ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING=False`, longer timeouts.

C. GNS3 auto-provisioning  (`backend/app/services/gns3_provisioner.py`, `backend/app/api/gns3.py`, hooks in `backend/app/api/devices.py`)
   - Env: `GNS3_AUTO_PROVISION`, `GNS3_URL` (default http://127.0.0.1:3080), `GNS3_USER/PASS`, `GNS3_PROJECT`
     (NetAutomation), `GNS3_SWITCH_TEMPLATE`, `GNS3_ROUTER_TEMPLATE`, `GNS3_CLOUD_INTERFACE`,
     `GNS3_MGMT_NETMASK`, `GNS3_BOOT_TIMEOUT`.
   - On device create (FastAPI BackgroundTasks): find/create project -> ensure `Mgmt-Cloud` (Windows Loopback adapter)
     + `Mgmt-Switch` (ethernet_switch) -> create node from template (name = device name) -> link to Mgmt-Switch
     -> start -> wait for console -> bootstrap over telnet console (hostname, mgmt IP = IP typed in the UI,
     local user, enable secret, SSH v2, RSA key, vty) -> status `Provisioning` -> audit log SUCCESS/FAILED.
   - On device delete: stop + delete the node.
   - Endpoints: `GET /api/gns3/status`, `POST /api/gns3/provision/{device_id}`.
   - Tested ONLY against a mock HTTP GNS3 server + fake IOS console, never against real GNS3.

D. Export  (`backend/app/services/export_engine.py`, `backend/app/api/export.py`)
   - `GET /api/export/page` (HTML with buttons), `GET /api/export/project?live=&include_gns3=` (ZIP),
     `GET /api/export/packet-tracer` (JS).
   - ZIP contains: `commands/<dev>_commands.txt` (paste-ready CLI), `commands/ALL_DEVICES_commands.txt`,
     `configs/<dev>.cfg` (+ `.source.txt`), `inventory.csv/json` (NO passwords), `deployment_history.csv`,
     `restore.py` (Netmiko re-apply), optional `gns3/*.gns3project`, and `packettracer/NetAutomation_PTBuilder.js`
     + how-to. Only the pure ZIP builder was unit-tested; the API layer was only compiled.

E. Packet Tracer  (`export_engine.packet_tracer_script`)
   - A real `.pkt` cannot be generated (closed/encrypted format). Instead we emit a script for the
     PTBuilder extension (github.com/kimmknight/PTBuilder): `addDevice`, `addLink`, `configurePcIp`,
     `configureIosDevice`. Never run against a real Packet Tracer.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. KNOWN GAPS / RISKS TO VERIFY FIRST (highest risk first)

1. GNS3 REST payloads (v2): cloud node `ports_mapping` + interface naming on Windows, template->node
   creation (`POST /v2/projects/{id}/templates/{tid}`), renaming, link creation, `console_host` 0.0.0.0 handling,
   start/stop. Also decide how to handle GNS3 3.x (JWT auth, `/v3` API) — detect version via `/version`
   and either support it or fail with a clear message.
2. Console bootstrap on IOSv / IOSvL2: initial-config dialog, `Press RETURN`, prompt regex, RSA key
   generation time, `ip domain-name` ordering, behaviour when the node is already configured (idempotency),
   telnet IAC handling, console already in use by another client.
3. IOSvL2 management: Gi0/0 is a switchport in VLAN 1 -> SVI `vlan 1` is used; confirm reachability
   from the Windows Loopback subnet (ARP, gateway, MTU). Confirm IOSv router `Gi0/0` addressing.
4. Device IP must be inside the Loopback subnet; validate it in the API and return a clear 400 if not
   (add env/setting for the Loopback IP/subnet).
5. Race: `Test Connection` / backup while the device is still `Provisioning`; status updates;
   duplicate provisioning if the user clicks twice; provisioning when GNS3 is closed (graceful error).
6. Export endpoints with the real DB: large configs, devices offline (3 s TCP pre-check), SIM mode,
   missing backup files, non-ASCII names, and `Content-Disposition` filenames.
7. PTBuilder script: confirm whether `configureIosDevice` adds `enable`/`configure terminal` itself
   (script currently omits them), valid port names for 2960-24TT / 2911, `crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024`
   support, link cable types, and that the file loads in the Builder Code Editor.
8. Frontend has NO UI for GNS3 provisioning status, re-provision, or export (only `/api/export/page`).
9. Topology links are NOT stored in the DB. Everything attaches to `Mgmt-Switch` only, so exports
   (GNS3 / PT / CLI) do not reflect a designed topology.
10. Ansible playbooks vs. dynamic inventory (groups `switches`/`routers`); Windows fallback path;
    deployment results parsing; `ansible_engine` fallback behaviour in real mode (must not hide failures).
11. Security: secrets encrypted at rest (`decrypt_secret`), no passwords in logs/exports, default creds
    `admin/cisco` used by the bootstrap (make configurable per device), CORS, auth on new endpoints
    (check whether other routers enforce auth and be consistent).
12. SQLite schema changes: `create_all` does not add columns to an existing DB — if you add columns,
    add a tiny migration (or Alembic) and keep the old `database.db` working.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. TARGET BEHAVIOUR (acceptance criteria)

Real mode (`run_gns3.bat`)
- [ ] `GET /api/gns3/status` shows GNS3 version, templates, host interfaces (or a clear error).
- [ ] Adding a Switch/Router in the UI creates a node in GNS3 project `NetAutomation`, linked via
      `Mgmt-Switch` <-> `Mgmt-Cloud`, started and bootstrapped; UI shows `Provisioning` then a final state.
- [ ] From Windows: `ping <device-ip>` and `ssh admin@<device-ip>` work.
- [ ] Test Connection = Online; Backup stores the real running-config; Deploy applies changes and they
      appear in the next backup; Drift detects a manual change made on the console; Verify reports honest PASS/FAIL.
- [ ] Deleting a device removes its GNS3 node. Re-provisioning an existing device works and is idempotent.
- [ ] Any failure (GNS3 closed, template missing, boot timeout, auth failure) is visible in the UI/Logs
      with an actionable message. No fake success anywhere.

Demo mode (`run.bat`): behaves exactly as the original project (mock devices) — no regression.

Export
- [ ] Project ZIP downloads from the UI and contains correct per-device CLI files; pasting
      `commands/<dev>_commands.txt` into a fresh IOS console reproduces the config.
- [ ] `restore.py` re-applies configs to GNS3 devices.
- [ ] PTBuilder script builds the topology in Packet Tracer and the devices respond to the config; document
      any command Packet Tracer's IOS rejects.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. CONSTRAINTS

- Do not log or export passwords/secrets. Keep device credentials encrypted in the DB.
- Real mode must never silently fall back to the simulator. Keep demo mode working behind `SIMULATOR_MODE=on`.
- Keep `backend/requirements.txt` accurate (add `requests` if missing, pin only if needed).
- Keep Windows compatibility (paths, `.bat` launchers with CRLF, no POSIX-only calls in backend code).
- Keep UI strings consistent with the existing UI language; support Arabic text in names/descriptions.
- Don't introduce heavy new dependencies without telling me why.
- Don't touch unrelated projects/files.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. TASKS — DO IN THIS ORDER

### Phase 1 — Understand & baseline
1. Read the whole repo; produce a 10-line architecture summary and confirm/correct section 2 and 3.
2. Create a virtualenv, install `backend/requirements.txt` (+ `requests`, `pytest`), start the backend in both
   modes; list anything that fails on startup.
3. Run the frontend build (`npm ci && npm run build` in `frontend/`) and confirm `dist` is served.

### Phase 2 — Tests first (no real GNS3 needed)
4. Add `backend/tests/` with pytest:
   - mock GNS3 HTTP server + fake IOS console (reuse the idea from section 2C) covering provisioner happy path,
     already-exists/idempotent path, GNS3 down, template missing, console timeout, switch full (7 ports);
   - `netmiko_engine` real-mode vs sim-mode behaviour (no fake success in real mode);
   - export: ZIP structure, no passwords, offline device fallback to last backup, PTBuilder script content;
   - API tests with FastAPI `TestClient` and a temp SQLite DB (devices CRUD hooks, `/api/export/*`, `/api/gns3/*`).
5. Fix every bug these reveal.

### Phase 3 — Real GNS3 integration (needs my machine)
6. Against my real GNS3 (2.2.x): run `/api/gns3/status`, then provision one IOSvL2 and one IOSv end to end.
   Fix payload / console / timing issues. Make bootstrap idempotent and tolerant of already-configured nodes.
7. Add: Loopback subnet validation, per-device credentials for bootstrap, clear error messages,
   cancel/retry of provisioning, protection against concurrent provisioning of the same device.
8. Handle GNS3 3.x (JWT) or fail with a precise message.
9. Verify the full lifecycle in section 4 (Test/Backup/Deploy/Drift/Verify/Delete).

### Phase 4 — Ansible & deployment path
10. Make the Ansible path work on Linux/WSL and clean fallback to Netmiko on Windows; make sure results are
    parsed into Deployment records accurately (SUCCESS/FAILED + message), no hidden failures.

### Phase 5 — Frontend
11. Add UI: provisioning status (poll every 5 s while `Provisioning`), "Re-provision in GNS3" action,
    GNS3 status indicator (server reachable? templates found?), and an "Export" page/menu with the 4 download
    options (live ZIP, offline ZIP, +GNS3 project, Packet Tracer script). Keep the existing design language.
12. Rebuild `frontend/dist` and make sure it is served.

### Phase 6 — Topology links (optional but valuable)
13. Add a `links` table (device A/port, device B/port) + CRUD API + simple UI. Make GNS3 provisioning,
    the GNS3 export, and the PTBuilder script use real links instead of only Mgmt-Switch.

### Phase 7 — Packet Tracer
14. Verify the PTBuilder script in Packet Tracer (I will run it if you give exact steps), fix API-semantics issues,
    document unsupported commands. Do NOT attempt to hand-build `.pkt` binaries.

### Phase 8 — Docs & delivery
15. Rewrite `docs/GNS3_SETUP.md` as a verified, step-by-step guide (Windows Loopback adapter, GNS3 templates,
    env vars, troubleshooting table for the top 10 errors).
16. Produce a final zip of the repo (exclude `node_modules`, caches) and a CHANGELOG.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. OUTPUT FORMAT

1. `PLAN` (short).
2. After each phase: `DONE`, `FILES CHANGED` (path + one line each), `COMMANDS RUN`, `RESULTS`.
3. Final report with three sections:
   - **Verified** (what you actually executed and saw working),
   - **Not verified** (needs my GNS3 / Packet Tracer / Windows machine, with exact steps for me),
   - **Open decisions** (questions for me).
4. Keep explanations concise; show code only when it clarifies a change.
